_about: Knowledge Definitions — the curated library of DEFINITIONS, not values. Stores the 'how' for Tiers 3-5 (Signal, Finding, Insight). Every entry re-derives fresh values from region_metrics whenever the data refreshes; nothing here is a stored result. Analyst-authored, version-controlled, auditable like code. See ANALYSIS_FRAMEWORK.md.

signal_templates._about: A Signal = a single comparative metric watched over time. Each template binds the four parameters {metric, period_type, lags, readout} to a name + interpretation. Values are produced on demand by a LAG/OVER window query over region_metrics; never precomputed here. 'lags' are calendar-month offsets (0 = now). 'readout': series = the lagged values; delta = value[0] - value[delta_lag]; slope = linear trend across lags.

mshare_deviation_mat.interpretation: Short- and medium-term trajectory of relative market-share position on a 12-month base: is the gap to national average closing or widening at -1M and -3M? Headline readouts are delta_1m (recent nudge) and delta_3m (quarter net). lags 1-3 give the full monthly step series so signal_strength can compute magnitude (total variation), net, and coherence. Feeds Turnaround / Deteriorating / Dangerous-Stability / Unstable recipes.

mshare_deviation_rollq.interpretation: RollQ Now vs RollQ -3Month: relative position shift across one full rolling-quarter window. The headline is delta_3m; lags 0-3 carry the full monthly step series so signal_strength can compute V/D/rho on the same 4-point basis as the MAT signals. NOTE: consecutive RollQ months overlap (each shares 2 of its 3 months with the next), so the step series is an autocorrelated/smoothed path, not independent observations. Window width (RollQ) and step back (LAG 3) remain the two orthogonal axes.

growth_py_sales_mat.interpretation: Trajectory of YoY sales growth on a 12-month base. The canonical '-10% now, -30% last month, -40% three months ago -> recovering' read. Positive slope = improving even when the level is still negative. NOTE: standardized to the 4-point monthly basis [0,1,2,3]; the previous -6M lag was dropped so this signal composes with the others. Restore lag 6 here if a longer momentum lookback is required.

growth_vs_fcst_eur_rollq.interpretation: Are we pulling toward or away from national forecast over the last quarter? Positive = converging on / beating plan; negative = falling behind plan.

growth_py_units_mat.interpretation: Volume-side counterpart to growth_py_sales momentum. Diverging unit vs value trajectories flag price/mix effects.

rank_sales_eur_mat.interpretation: Change in volume rank over 3 periods. The headline delta_3m is unchanged by the added lags 1-2, which only enrich the series for signal_strength on the standard 4-point basis. NOTE: the headline delta is cached in region_metrics as rank_trend_3m for performance — a materialized hot signal, not a separate definition; the cache stores the lag-3 delta only, so adding intermediate lags does not affect it.

growth_pp_mshare_dev_month.interpretation: Period-over-period change in market-share deviation. A 'growth-of-growth' column — the comparison's own change is already baked into region_metrics. Standardized to the 4-point monthly basis [0,1,2,3]: lag 0 is the headline pp value (also cached as growth_pp_mshare_dev), and lags 1-3 give its recent history so signal_strength can read a trajectory on the same basis as every other signal.

growth_deviation_mat.interpretation: Region's YoY sales growth minus the brand's volume-weighted national YoY growth (PY), on a 12-month base — is the region out-growing or under-growing the brand overall, and is that gap widening? Peer-relative growth-momentum companion to mshare_deviation; together they place a region in the share x growth quadrant.

growth_deviation_rollq.interpretation: RollQ counterpart to growth_deviation_mat: region YoY sales growth minus the brand's volume-weighted national YoY growth, on a rolling-quarter base rather than 12-month. More responsive to recent swings than the MAT version. NOTE: consecutive RollQ months overlap (each shares 2 of its 3 months with the next), so the step series is an autocorrelated/smoothed path, not independent observations.

signal_roles._about: Named references from code and UI to signal_templates, so the chosen signal id is resolved from config at runtime instead of hard-coded in source. Each value MUST be a key in signal_templates (validated by knowledge.py). Add a role here rather than embedding a template id in a .py/.html/.ts file.

finding_recipes._about: A Finding = open-ended composition of lower facts (usually several signals). Each recipe is method-agnostic: 'rule' here is a human-readable predicate an engine OR an LLM can evaluate. 'requires_signals' lists the signal templates that feed it; 'gap' refers to value vs brand peer-median, 'momentum' to the signal's direction (WIDENING/STABLE/SHRINKING for growth; IMPROVING/STABLE/DECLINING for position). Thresholds come from relevance.magnitude.

star.label: Star
star.rule: mshare_deviation now >= 0  AND  growth_deviation now >= 0 (ahead on both).
star.description: Ahead of the peer average on both share and growth. Healthy.
star.default_action: Sustain; learn what's working to replicate.

slowing_giant.label: Slowing Giant
slowing_giant.rule: growth_gap > 0 AND growth_momentum == SHRINKING AND position_momentum == DECLINING
slowing_giant.description: Still above peers but momentum turning negative; execution needs focus.
slowing_giant.default_action: Investigate cause of slowdown before position deteriorates further.

turnaround.label: Turnaround
turnaround.rule: position_gap < 0 AND position_momentum == IMPROVING AND persistence >= 3_periods
turnaround.description: Was below/far below median, now recovering on a consistent multi-period trajectory.
turnaround.default_action: Support what's working; continue momentum-building actions.

deteriorating.label: Deteriorating
deteriorating.rule: growth_gap < 0 AND growth_momentum == SHRINKING AND position_momentum == DECLINING
deteriorating.description: Dual problem: structural underperformance + worsening trend + likely forecast miss.
deteriorating.default_action: Diagnose root cause (execution, market, staffing); consider intervention.

riding_wave.label: Riding the Wave
riding_wave.description: Strong absolute numbers but not outpacing peers; national market booming.
riding_wave.default_action: Good for revenue; if share growth is the goal, need a differentiation strategy.

weak_foundation.label: Weak Foundation
weak_foundation.description: Growing at a healthy rate but not catching up to peers; secondary market.
weak_foundation.default_action: Viable if efficiency is the goal; major investment needed to elevate to strategic status.

dangerous_stability.label: Dangerous Stability
dangerous_stability.description: No alarm bells in growth but slowly losing market edge to competitors.
dangerous_stability.default_action: Proactive competitive response needed to reverse the trend.

unstable.label: Unstable / Erratic
unstable.rule: signal.magnitude >= loud AND abs(signal.coherence) < 0.3   (big total variation, near-zero net — the position is swinging hard but going nowhere)
unstable.description: Volatility itself is the finding: high loudness, ~zero coherence (e.g. -10 then +10). Reading a trend into it would be wrong — there is no net direction.
unstable.default_action: Check data quality, demand spikiness, or stocking/ordering noise before treating any single point as a trend.

finding_recipes._share_x_growth: Region findings on the SHARE × GROWTH quadrant: position = mshare_deviation, momentum = growth_deviation (both vs volume-weighted national). Quadrant by current level; severity = ms_sev + growth_sev (each 0-3). No FCST at region level. Impl: findings.py.

losing_both.label: Losing on both
losing_both.rule: mshare_deviation now < 0  AND  growth_deviation now < 0  (below peers on share AND growth). Severity rises if either axis is deteriorating / loud.
losing_both.description: Below the peer average on BOTH market share and growth — the red cell. Losing position and not out-growing to recover.
losing_both.default_action: Diagnose; this is where real share is bleeding. Check accounts.

slipping.label: Slipping
slipping.rule: mshare_deviation now >= 0 (ahead on share)  AND  growth_deviation now < 0 (under-growing).
slipping.description: Still ahead on share but growing slower than the brand — momentum is turning. A strong position starting to erode.
slipping.default_action: Protect the position before the share lead is spent.

catching_up.label: Catching up
catching_up.rule: mshare_deviation now < 0 (below on share)  AND  growth_deviation now >= 0 (out-growing).
catching_up.description: Below the peer average on share but out-growing the brand — closing the gap. Recovering, low concern.

insight_framings._about: An Insight = a Finding + business context for ONE persona. Each framing declares the persona's scope and cadence, WHICH findings to surface, when to STAY SILENT, and how to phrase it. The same finding yields a different insight per persona — or none at all. 'surface_when'/'suppress_when' are predicates over a finding's archetype, strength, and materiality.

sales_manager.label: Sales Manager
sales_manager.decision: Builds the monthly plan with each rep across all territories.
sales_manager.surface_when: strength >= moderate AND materiality >= medium  (anything plan-relevant in any territory)
sales_manager.phrasing_guide: Frame as where to spend the rep's attention this month. Recovery -> 'rep on track to recover an important region, keep it on the plan'.
sales_manager.territory_overview: Lead each territory with an overall verdict from territory-level metrics (YoY growth, plan attainment): e.g. 'Bern looks healthy — growing YoY and beating plan — but N regions worth addressing.' A healthy territory can still hide troubled regions, so always pair the headline with the exceptions.
sales_manager.reminders: The manager can't recall last month's report, so mark each region's month-over-month status: ✓ improved since last month; ↻ flagged again (red now and last month); ‼ red 3 consecutive months (unresolved). Also list regions that recovered out of the report since last month.
sales_manager.show_rank: Every region mentioned carries its sales rank (rank_sales_eur percentile) so the manager can weigh it.

sales_rep.label: Sales Rep
sales_rep.decision: Works every region of their own territory in detail.
sales_rep.surface_when: territory == rep.territory  (everything in my patch, in detail)
sales_rep.phrasing_guide: Always give a next action. Recovery -> 'turnaround possible, keep pushing; check all accounts for order status'.

ceo.label: CEO
ceo.decision: Wants a picture of the MOST PROBLEMATIC regions and territories.
ceo.surface_when: territory has bigger regions (high materiality) red 3 months running, OR the territory itself is behind plan / deteriorating on share
ceo.suppress_when: archetype in [star, turnaround, riding_wave] OR direction == improving  (an improving region is NOT a problem -> silence)
ceo.phrasing_guide: Only escalate true problems with scale. A recovering region produces NO insight for the CEO — suppression is the correct output.
ceo.escalation: Escalate at the TERRITORY level — the Product × Territory view is granular enough for the board. A territory enters the CEO report if it has bigger regions flagged red for 3 consecutive months (rep & manager did not resolve them), or if the territory's own metrics are behind plan or its share is deteriorating. The report names the territory, its product/territory metrics, and the COUNT of bigger regions red for the 3rd month (‼) — individual region detail stays with the rep & manager.
ceo.order: Always ordered by territory size (largest € first) so the board can stop reading once territories get immaterial. Bigger regions red for the 3rd month are named in brackets — a reference for the CEO↔Sales-Manager meeting.

signal_strength._about: INTRINSIC loudness + shape of a signal's trajectory — a property of the signal itself, independent of whether the region matters for business. Computed over the consecutive step-deltas of the metric across the signal's window (values oldest -> now). Keep all three measures; do not collapse to one scalar.
signal_strength.magnitude: V = sum(|step deltas|) — total variation / path length / LOUDNESS. Always >= 0, in metric units (pp). Answers 'how much did it move in total'. (This is the unsigned 'sum of deltas'.)
signal_strength.net: D = value_now - value_start = signed sum of steps (telescopes). DIRECTION: sign(D) read through the template's 'direction' (higher_is_better) => improving / deteriorating. Answers 'where did it end up'.
signal_strength.coherence: rho = D / V, in [-1, +1]. TREND vs OSCILLATION. |rho| -> 1 = monotone clean move; rho -> 0 = loud oscillation that nets to nothing (e.g. -10 then +10: V=20, D=0, rho=0). This is the signed Kaufman Efficiency Ratio. It is why V and D must both be kept: V catches the oscillation D hides, sign(D) gives the direction V lacks.
signal_strength.signed_strength: D * |rho| — convenience scalar: net displacement discounted by incoherence. Equals net for a perfectly clean trend, -> 0 for a pure oscillation. Use for sorting; never as a replacement for the three measures.

loudness_bands_pp._note: Buckets for V (and for |net|). pp thresholds; choose ladder by metric kind.

coherence_bands._note: |rho| >= trend => clean trend; |rho| < oscillation => oscillation; between => mixed.

shapes.trend: V >= loud AND |rho| >= trend       -> clean directional move (feeds Turnaround / Deteriorating)
shapes.unstable: V >= loud AND |rho| <  oscillation -> loud but going nowhere net (feeds Unstable)

relevance._about: EXTRINSIC filter — does a (loud) signal land somewhere that MATTERS for business? Separate from signal_strength: a signal can be loud and clean yet irrelevant (tiny region), or quiet yet relevant. relevance = materiality * loudness * horizon. Coherence does NOT enter relevance; it selects WHICH finding archetype (trend vs unstable).

loudness_by_V._note: Banded from signal_strength.loudness_bands_pp for the metric kind.
